title: Responder: your account, availability, and security
audience: Individual members, volunteers, responders, and supervisors using their own account.
summary: Learn which identity Responder represents, sign in on the correct server, set personal status and staffing, and protect access to departmental information.
prerequisites: An isolated training department, a member account, configured personnel statuses and staffing levels, and sample calls, stations, and POIs.
A second demonstration session for approval; SSO, MFA, and passkeys configured only for the corresponding optional branches.
A native device for platform permission demonstrations. Show browser differences explicitly; capture plans are not proof of delivered notifications or working hardware.

scenes.capture_intent: Use the referenced actual application viewports in their listed order. Keep credentials out of the recording and retain all declared platform/configuration limits.
scenes.narration: Responder is the personal workspace for a named member. Check the account and department, then read My Status and My Staffing on Home. People, Units, and Calls provide the wider operating picture. A community response team can use the same pattern to show who is available and which incident each person is joining. Every name and incident shown here belongs to our fictional training department.

source_workflow_reference.narration: Responder follows you as an individual member. On Home, the Status, Staffing, and Call tabs answer three different questions: what you are doing, whether you are available, and which incident you are following. Your department may use different terminology. Read the actual labels before changing anything, and keep personal availability separate from the status of a vehicle shared by a crew.

Read a few labels after changing it so you recognize the same workflow in that language.

scenes.narration: Use Change Server URL before signing in when your organization supplies a different API endpoint. Return to Username and Password, then Login using your own authorized account. Keep credentials outside screenshots and shared recordings.

source_workflow_reference.narration: Before entering credentials, select Change Server URL and confirm the server or region your department uses. Choose a listed location or Custom, then save the address. Return to Username and Password and select Login. A correct password on the wrong server can still fail. Keep your credentials private and use the training account while practicing this server-selection workflow.

A deployed organization must verify its provider, return link, and any additional challenge on the intended platform before relying on that sign-in path.

source_workflow_reference.narration: If your organization provides single sign-on, choose Login with SSO and enter the username requested by the discovery screen. Continue through the organization sign-in shown for that account, then return to Responder. If no configuration is found, use Back and the permitted password route. Browser callbacks and native app redirects differ, so show the actual return path on the platform being taught.

source_workflow_reference.narration: When sign-in asks for another factor, use a method that is actually offered for this account. An authenticator code, passkey, and approval request are different choices, not interchangeable promises. Recover your account is for a lost factor: a recovery code starts replacement and can end existing sessions. Use Continue only on a disposable training account when demonstrating that recovery path.

scenes.title: Set a personal status deliberately

scenes.narration: On Home, select Status and read the offered choices before changing your personal state. This department offers Responding, Not Responding, On Scene, and Standing By. Its labels and transitions come from department configuration. The example selects Responding and opens Set Status: Responding. After the completed action, My Status shows the saved state and destination. Use the displayed result to confirm the change.

source_workflow_reference.narration: Open Status and read the option marked Current. To set a quick status, press and hold the chosen button for two seconds. The available next steps follow your department’s configured workflow. Show all statuses exposes additional choices, while Show next statuses only returns to the guided list. Choose a status because it describes your activity; do not use it as a substitute for staffing availability.

scenes.narration: The destination step separates Calls, Stations, and POI. Select the intended destination before moving to Add Note. In this exercise, the community medical standby is the chosen call and the note clearly says it is an Academy exercise. Save completes the personal status change, and the Home card displays that destination. Read any required-field instruction in your department rather than assuming every status uses the same steps.

source_workflow_reference.narration: Some statuses open a destination step. Select Calls, Stations, or POI when offered, and choose the incident or place you mean. In this training account, the POI list is empty. Add the requested note, review the confirmation, and select Save. Check the resulting personal status and destination on Home. A successful card update does not establish that an offline update has synchronized to every device.

scenes.title: Keep staffing availability accurate
scenes.capture_intent: Use the referenced actual application viewports in their listed order. Keep credentials out of the recording and retain all declared platform/configuration limits.
scenes.narration: Staffing records your availability for assignment. This department offers Available, Delayed, Unavailable, Committed, and On Shift. The example chooses Available, uses Add Note to state the training availability window, and checks Review and Confirm before Submit. My Staffing then shows the saved result. Personal status and staffing serve different coordination needs, so read both cards when handing over a community care or search-team duty period.

source_workflow_reference.narration: Open Staffing when you need to tell the department whether you can help. A quick staffing choice may apply immediately, while a long press opens the note flow. Some choices require a note before confirmation. Use Add Note to explain a useful limit, such as an availability window, and review the resulting staffing card. Staffing describes availability even when your activity status has not changed.

scenes.title: Approve only the request you started
scenes.capture_intent: Use the referenced actual application viewports in their listed order. Keep credentials out of the recording and retain all declared platform/configuration limits.
scenes.narration: Responder approvals lists device approval availability; this account shows Approvals stopped. A configured approval request must be matched to a sign-in you initiated, including its number, before any approval. No challenge or hardware notification was exercised here. For a shared or handed-over device, Logout asks for confirmation before clearing local session data. The declared web recording adapter preserves the source confirmation text and buttons; native confirmation remains platform-specific.

source_workflow_reference.narration: Responder can show Approve sign-in? for a request started in another Resgrid session. Compare the app, department, device label, location context, and expiration. Enter the Number shown on the requesting screen, then complete the offered passkey verification before choosing Approve. Choose Deny for an unexpected request. Check the requesting session afterward, because approving a request and reaching a signed-in workspace are separate states.

sector_examples.scenario: A fire or EMS member checks in before a fictional standby.
sector_examples.practice: Confirm the actual signed-in member and department, select only a personal status/destination and required note, and keep personal staffing separate from apparatus status or crew assignment.

sector_examples.scenario: A mobile crisis or community-care responder makes availability clear.
sector_examples.practice: Use the actual personal status and staffing screens with a fictional note; keep real client or health details out of training data and verify the displayed result.

sector_examples.scenario: A SAR volunteer prepares for a staging assignment.
sector_examples.practice: Read the actual Calls, Stations and POIs destination choices offered for the selected status; a software destination is not proof of GPS tracking, arrival or dispatch receipt.

sector_examples.scenario: A security officer begins a patrol shift.
sector_examples.practice: Check personal identity, current availability and the People/Units picture. Inspect sign-in verification choices and recent activity without enrolling credentials or changing another member.

sector_examples.scenario: A wildland mutual-aid member reviews access and readiness.
sector_examples.practice: Confirm the intended server/account and personal availability; use only offered recovery or approval controls. Browser security/settings views do not demonstrate native communications or location hardware.

sector_examples.scenario: An industrial response member uses the personal app alongside a vehicle tablet.
sector_examples.practice: Distinguish Responder member status/staffing from Unit apparatus/crew context. Read actual passkey/authenticator/approval states and verify a request before acting, with no MFA or device credential changes.

capture_limitations: No native push delivery, authenticator challenge, passkey operation, recovery-code use, device approval, GPS, Bluetooth or provider success is claimed.
SSO provider discovery is unconfigured; the real entry screen and no-challenge recovery prerequisite are shown.
